findings.problem: The term 'talla superior' (higher height/taller) is the opposite of the intended meaning. In the context of an underweight child, the clinician should use a lower weight estimate, which corresponds to the row 'above' (shorter height) in the chart. 'Talla superior' would lead a clinician to use a taller child's weight, potentially causing a medication overdose.
findings.fix: o **1 categoría de talla inferior** (p. ej., bajo peso con 100 cm — use **11–12 kg**)
findings.en:
**Underweight:** use **2 age-categories younger** (e.g. an underweight
10-month-old — use the weight for 4–6 months) or **1 height-category
above** (e.g. underweight at 100 cm — use **11–12 kg**).
findings.es:
**Bajo peso:** use **2 categorías de edad menores** (p. ej., para un lactante de 10 meses
con bajo peso — use el peso de 4–6 meses) o **1 categoría de talla
superior** (p. ej., bajo peso con 100 cm — use **11–12 kg**).
